en.title: Sweet Hamster Days: GTA V Meets Hamster Life in Bizarre FMV Sim
en.summary: A peculiar FMV game where you play as a reincarnated hamster being pampered by three sisters has finally found its footing on Steam. This unique 'being-taken-care-of adventure game' draws inspiration from unexpected places.
en.body:
Forget saving the world or building empires; sometimes, the most compelling gaming experiences involve being a pampered hamster. **Sweet Hamster Days**, a live-action romance sim, lets players step into the tiny paws of Hamta, a hamster doted upon by three devoted Japanese sisters. This isn't your typical visual novel; it's a genre-bending adventure that emerged from a developer's surprisingly relatable past experiences.

The game's overseer, **Katayama**, revealed that the core concept was sparked by his time working part-time in an animal mascot costume. He observed how the costume broke down social barriers, making people, especially children and the elderly, more approachable. This realization about connection and perceived identity laid the groundwork for a game where a beloved pet could foster unique relationships.

Adding another layer to this already unconventional idea is inspiration from **Grand Theft Auto V**. "I'm a big fan of Grand Theft Auto 5," Katayama explained, "where you switch between three protagonists as you progress. As I was having fun switching between the lives of other people, lives that weren't my own, I had this idea that it might be nice to have a hamster as one of the options instead of a human." This juxtaposition of high-octane, multi-protagonist gameplay with the gentle, nurturing premise of **Sweet Hamster Days** is certainly unexpected.

## A Genre All Its Own

**Sweet Hamster Days** positions itself as a "completely unprecedented genre," a "being-taken-care-of adventure game." Players embody Hamta, the pet of the Shiratori sisters, who spend their days gazing lovingly at the camera and seemingly showering their furry companion with affection. The narrative tasks players with mending a rift that has grown between the sisters, using Hamta's "tiny paws and big heart." The game's journey to Steam wasn't entirely smooth; it was initially rejected, with the development team revising details like age rating settings before its eventual approval.

## The Appeal of the Unconventional

The boom of FMV dating sims in Asia, particularly in China, also played a significant role in the game's development, as noted by designer **Oda**. This trend highlights a growing player appetite for unique, character-focused experiences that leverage live-action visuals. For fans of visual novels and simulation games, **Sweet Hamster Days** offers a refreshing departure from typical human-centric narratives, inviting players into a world of simple pleasures and heartfelt connections, albeit from a very small perspective.

## What's Next

While the initial Steam listing mentioned a July 2026 launch, details regarding the final release date and any further platform availability for **Sweet Hamster Days** have not yet been officially announced.

content_raw: Sweet Hamster Days was initially rejected by Steam, perhaps because Valve is more restrictive of games that feature sexually explicit images of real people , or possibly for some other reason we'll never know. As a designer called Oda told Automaton , "We still don’t know exactly how the platform saw things, but after revising details such as the age rating settings and re-submitting the game, it was eventually approved." This is an FMV game where you die and are reincarnated as a hamster named Hamta, the pet of three sisters who seem to spend most of their time gazing lovingly into the camera while pretending to pat you on the head. "We're calling it a completely unprecedented genre," Oda said, "a kind of 'being-taken-care-of adventure game.'" The project's overseer, who goes by Katayama, gave some insight into the conception of this deeply strange idea for a game. "Years ago, I worked a part-time job wearing mascot costumes. I realized that whenever I wore a costume, children and elderly people who would normally never approach me suddenly became very friendly", he said. The other half of the idea came from a videogame, though not one with an obvious link to an FMV visual novel about hamster-pampering. "I'm a big fan of Grand Theft Auto 5," Katayama went on to say, "where you switch between three protagonists as you progress. As I was having fun switching between the lives of other people, lives that weren't my own, I had this idea that it might be nice to have a hamster as one of the options instead of a human." Well, that makes perfect sense then. The more prosaic reason for Sweet Hamster Days being made is the boom of FMV dating sims in Asia . "Katayama had mentioned to me that live-action games were becoming popular in China," Oda said. The Road to Empress series was a recent FMV hit to come out of China, and Korea's Five Hearts Under One Roof has also been quite popular. It's only natural a Japanese studio would want to get in on the action, and I guess making your game about someone being turned into a hamster by Truck-kun is one way to stand out. Sweet Hamster Days is available now on Steam and the Epic Games Store .
